bihar_raw_news.title: From Himalayan flash flood to Malda's eroding banks: How India averted a dangerous river surge
bihar_raw_news.content: A potentially dangerous flood wave triggered by a devastating flash flood in Nepal appears to have been contained on the Indian side through intensive river monitoring and regulated barrage operations, averting an immediate large-scale flood threat in parts of Bihar and West Bengal. The chain of events began on August 26, when the water level of Nepal’s Trishuli river rose sharply following a flash-flood event near the Nepal-Tibet border. Advertisement The Central Water Commission (CWC), under the Ministry of Jal Shakti, issued an advisory to Bihar and Uttar Pradesh, warning that a flood wave could travel downstream through the Gandak River system. Advertisement The National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) was subsequently placed on high alert. The hydrological significance of the event lay in the interconnected river system. The Trishuli and Kali Gandaki meet at Devghat in Nepal to form the Narayani, which enters India as the Gandak and flows through Bihar before joining the Ganga system. In response, Bihar authorities opened all 36 gates of the Gandak Barrage at Valmikinagar to regulate the surge. Around 38 lakh cusecs of water were released over 22 hours. The latest data from the Bihar Water Resources Department showed the Valmikinagar Gandak Barrage releasing around 1.50 lakh cusecs, while the Kosi Barrage was releasing about 1.56 lakh cusecs. Both figures remained substantially below their respective designed discharge capacities. The downstream Ganga system, including the Farakka Barrage, was also kept under close watch. A senior engineer of the West Bengal Irrigation Department said the immediate flood threat to northern West Bengal had eased. “There is no immediate possibility of flooding in West Bengal,” the engineer told The Statesman. “However, if there is substantial rainfall in the upper catchment in the coming days, the situation could be different,” he added. River levels along parts of the Ganga between Varanasi and Sahibganj have also shown a declining trend, officials said. In Malda, the Ganga stood at around 25.17 metres on Sunday morning and fell marginally to 25.16 metres by 1pm. “In 2023, when a glacial lake outburst in Sikkim triggered a flash flood, we followed the same approach and safely passed the excess water through the Teesta,” chief engineer, North-East Krishnendu Bhowmik told The Statesman. “This time too, we adopted a similar strategy, allowing the additional water to flow through the Ganga. As a result, a flood-like situation did not develop in North Bengal,” he added. Though the receding water level has eased the immediate flood threat, it has heightened the risk of renewed erosion along the vulnerable riverbanks of Ratua and adjoining areas. The retreating Ganga has already swallowed a portion of a primary school and poses a growing threat to several villages along its banks. Several villages have been facing sustained erosion for weeks, with residents losing homes and agricultural land. With the monsoon still active and the possibility of heavy rainfall in the upper catchments through September and into early October, officials remain cautious about the longer-term situation. bihar_raw_news.title: Finance ministry to begin preparing for Budget 2027-28 from October 12 - The Pioneer
bihar_raw_news.content: August 30, 2026 Finance ministry to begin preparing for Budget 2027-28 from October 12 Copy Link X WhatsApp Share By Pioneer News Service The Finance Ministry will begin the exercise to prepare the Union Budget for 2027-28 from October 12 amid heightened global uncertainties and rising food and fuel prices. The Budget for the next financial year is expected to focus on the reform continuation exercise to further accelerate economic growth, along with measures to create jobs and boost domestic demand. “Pre-budget meetings chaired by Secretary (Expenditure) shall commence from October 12, 2026. Financial Advisers shall ensure that necessary details... are properly entered in UBIS (Union Budget Information System) before/latest by October 6, 2026,” Budget circular 2027-28 issued by the Department of Economic Affairs said. Hard copies of the data in the specified formats should be submitted for cross-verification, it said. It will be the fourth Budget of the Modi 3.0 Government and the 10th straight Budget for Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman, a rare distinction in Indian polity. The circular further said that pre-budget meetings would commence from October 12, 2026, and continue till mid-November 2026. The Budget Estimates for 2027-28, as well as Revised Estimates for 2026-27, will be provisionally finalised after completion of pre-Budget meetings, it added. After detailed discussions in the pre-budget meetings, provisional expenditure ceilings will be indicated to the ministries/departments, it said. Final expenditure ceilings will be decided by the ministry after factoring in the expenditure priorities and receipt projections of the Government, it said. The final expenditure figures would be transmitted through and reflected in the UBIS latest by end-December 2026/early-January 2027, it added. It further said that estimates of central taxes and duties, including surcharges and cesses, should be furnished by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) to the Budget Division. 0 Likes 0 Dislikes Bookmark 0 Comments Leave a Comment

bihar_raw_news.title: Government notification issued in 2005 can't be applied retrospectively, rules Patna High Court
bihar_raw_news.content: Widow loses family pension after 7 years: Government notification issued in 2005 can’t be applied retrospectively, rules Patna High Court ET Online Widow’s family pension stopped after 7 years payment as Bihar Govt’s beneficial 2005 notification can’t be applied retrospectively (AI generated representative image) Synopsis Govt employee died in a naxalite bomb blast in 2003. His widow received an ex gratia payment and a seven-year family pension. She sought an extended pension based on a 2005 government policy. The Patna High Court ruled the policy could not be applied retrospectively. Read the article to know more. By Neelanjit Das , ET Online Aug 30, 2026, 07:00:00 AM IST Follow us On September 5, 1994, Mr Kumar from Kathiyar was appointed as a sub-inspector (SI) of police and his tentative retirement date was May 31, 2027. However, on September 8, 2003, he died from a naxalite bomb blast while being posted at Tilathou Police Station in Rohtas. The police after investigation (case no. 36/2003) also ruled that his death was caused by a naxalite bomb blast. ADVERTISEMENT Consequently, on the recommendation of the Superintendent of Police (SP), Rohtas and the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Shahabad Range, an ex gratia payment of Rs 10 lakh was given to his wife Smt Kumari on November 21, 2003. The SP, Rohtas also recommended that Kumari (the widow) be given a family pension for seven years (September 9, 2003 till September 8, 2010). So, she started getting a family pension which was stopped on September 8, 2010 as per the SP’s recommendation. This created a problem and as Kumari needed funds, she requested the authorities to extend the pension. She filed multiple representations, applications and ultimately went to court seeking extension of the family pension. Her argument was based on a 2005 Bihar government policy notification which had extended special/extraordinary pension to all government employees who died in harness due to an act of violence. This notification had removed the previous seven-year cap. Also read: Enhanced family pension: Parents of deceased govt employees must file separate life certificates to get pension at higher rate The problem is this 2005 notification is progressive and could not be applied retrospectively. ADVERTISEMENT Therefore, she ultimately lost the case in Patna High Court on April 20, 2026. The Patna High Court ruled that a beneficial executive policy of the Bihar government cannot be applied retrospectively to her case in the absence of express provision, and reiterated that courts cannot expand the scope of a scheme beyond its stated terms. The Patna High Court said that it is necessary to examine the nature and scope of the Bihar government resolution dated November 12, 2005, an executive policy decision. The 2005 resolution extended the benefit of special/extraordinary family pension earlier confined to police personnel to all government employees dying in harness due to violent acts, and removed the upper cap of seven years by extending the benefit till the date of retirement. national_raw_news.title: 11 mins ago | National 5 PM Modi holds delegation-level talks with Uzbekistan’s President Shavkat Mirziyoyev in Tashkent
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that India and Uzbekistan are elevating their ties to the level of a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. In his opening remarks during delegation-level talks with President Shavkat Mirziyoyev, the Prime Minister said both countries will move forward by setting concrete goals within the framework of the elevated partnership. Prime Minister Modi said both countries also established a long-term arrangement for the supply of uranium. He said the two countries are also formalising three sister-city and sister-state arrangements. He said both countries will establish a Coordination Council at the Foreign Minister level to provide direction to all aspects of bilateral cooperation through close coordination. Mr Modi said Joint Commission will be elevated to the Ministerial level from the Secretary level. He said, both sides will also jointly organise a business summit featuring business leaders from both the nations. Mr Modi also expressed happiness over the coincidence of their 15th anniversary of strategic partnership and 35th anniversary of Independence Day of Uzbekistan. Mr Modi also extended advance congratulations and best wishes to the people of Uzbekistan on the occasion of their Independence Day, which falls on 1st of September. In his opening remarks during the talks President Mirziyoyev said India is achieving remarkable results across all sectors, maintaining high rates of economic growth and implementing major projects. He said India is making truly outstanding advances in digitalisation, information technology, artificial intelligence, space exploration, and many other fields. Mirziyoyev said, New Delhi’s voice and influence in global affairs have grown even stronger and he is pleased to see all these achievements.

national_raw_news.title: 60 mins ago | National 178 Mann Ki Baat programme: PM Modi highlights women empowerment through PM SVANidhi
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi has said that the ‘Nasha-mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat’ campaign is gaining momentum rapidly across the country. Sharing his thoughts in the Mann Ki Baat programme on Akashvani this morning, Mr Modi expressed happiness that the campaign with the goal for drug-free youth and a drug-free India is not merely a formality, as many people, especially the youth are joining it in large numbers. He said, this is the collective resolve for the health, happiness, and bright future of India’s youth. The Prime Minister said, drug addiction does not just engulf a single individual but the entire family and society bear the consequences. He commended those who raise awareness against drugs and step forward to help individuals struggling with addiction. Mr Modi asked people to come up with a powerful slogan for a drug-free India and young musicians to create songs that convey the message of a drug-free life. He said, the country has no shortage of excellent content creators. Mr Modi urged them to create content in various languages to help society in this endeavor. He said, they can use their creativity as a medium for social change. The Prime Minister said, lakhs of women are gaining new strength through the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. He said, this aspect of ‘women empowerment’ is not discussed as much as it should be. Mr Modi said, Women account for approximately 46 percent of the beneficiaries of the ‘PM SVANidhi Yojana’. Ningamma from Bengaluru who have benefited from the scheme. He said, when a woman’s business grows, the future of her entire family advances along with it, children receive a better education, household needs are met, and the woman’s self-confidence is strengthened. He said, this is, indeed, a living example of women’s empowerment. The Prime Minister said cleanliness has a remarkable quality. He said, when the resolve to keep a place clean becomes the people’s own commitment, it completely changes the identity of that place. Mr Modi said, such efforts towards cleanliness in various parts of the country constantly inspire people. He mentioned Akash and Rohan of Patwai in Uttar Pradesh, who inspired others to clean up public places, including river ghats. The Prime Minister also spoke about Shri Amarnath Yatra where more than 400 metric tonnes of waste was collected and processed. He said, Maithili Bhue of Dhodrokusum in the Debrigarh region of Odisha has shown that it is possible to protect nature while also achieving prosperity in life. Mr Modi said, today the flight of the country’s daughters’ dreams is soaring from the earth to outer space. He said, India is bringing together thousands of daughters who are nurturing such dreams from across the globe.’ The Prime Minister said, the initiative is named ‘Mission ShaktiSAT, and through it, 12 thousand girl students from 108 countries are getting the opportunity to learn satellite technology in the field of innovation. He said, on National Space Day this month, a wonderful glimpse of this mission was seen in Greater Noida, Uttar Pradesh where the second phase of Mission ShaktiSAT was launched at the Gautam Buddha University. Mr Modi mentioned how Varadaraj from Kadappa in Andhra Pradesh, Chandrashekharan from Kodaikanal in Tamil Nadu are cultivating avocados and earning additional income. Mr Modi spoke to Krishna Sheshadri from Mumbai who has created a unique website www.bharatrajya.com. By selecting any year in the website people can easily find out which ruler ruled over which part of India at that time. He said, this initiative by Mr Krishna will help not only history students but people to learn about the past in an engaging way. The Prime Minister said, the month of August brought with it myriad hues of patriotism all around. He said, occasions such as ‘National Handloom Day’ and the anniversary of the ‘Quit India Movement’ to ‘Partition Horrors Remembrance Day’ make this month special. national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 254 Nepal Flash Floods: Death toll rises to 734; Nearly 2,500 still missing
national_raw_news.content: The death toll from flash floods in central Nepal has risen to 734 today, with more bodies being recovered. Nearly 2,500 people are still missing following the disaster. Bodies have been recovered from all eight affected districts as rescuers race against time to search for those missing and rescue those stranded on the fifth day since the disaster. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) of Nepal said, so far, 259 dead bodies have been recovered from Chitwan, 184 from Nawalparasi East, 82 from Nawalparasi West and 58 from Gorkha districts. Similarly, 52 bodies have been recovered from Nuwakot, 50 from Dhading, 36 from Tanahu and 13 from Rasuwa. It said that 2,498 people are also missing, including 85 security personnel and 320 foreigners. Rescuers have so far evacuated 8,186 people from the affected districts, including 227 foreigners, it said. The Nepal government has issued fresh alert for flood in Bhote Koshi River and urged residents living along the river to remain cautious. NDRRMA has reported an increased flood flow in the river. Rasuwa District Administration has advised people in areas near the Bhote Koshi River in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts to exercise caution. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that 108 Indian nationals have been rescued so far in Nepal following flash flood tragedy. In a social media post, Mr Jaiswal said that contact was re-established with around 50 Indian nationals who were earlier uncontactable. The External Affairs Ministry said that 275 Indian nationals are reportedly missing and around 128 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities, also remain missing. As per local government source, 598 Indian nationals crossed into Nepal from China in the last two days. Meanwhile, 900 Indian nationals who are yet to depart from China are safe and the Indian Embassy in Beijing is in touch with them directly or through the local government. The Ministry added that Government of India has been working in close coordination with the Nepali and Chinese authorities for the early rescue and relief efforts of those affected by the floods. India is continuously supporting the relief and rescue operation in flash flood hit Nepal. The 4th flight carrying 11 tonnes of relief assistance has landed in Kathmandu, and relief material has been handed over to Nepal government. In a social media post, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that the flight carried essential supplies and technical capabilities to support Nepal’s ongoing rescue and relief operations. Earlier, India had sent more than 57 tonnes of emergency relief supplies in three flights.An ice-rock avalanche following a glacial collapse near the Nepal-Tibet border sent a torrent of water, mud and debris downstream. It wiped out towns and villages, damaging crucial infrastructure and washing away hydropower stations through central Nepal on Wednesday.

national_raw_news.title: IMD forecasts extremely heavy rainfall in Odisha today 2 hours ago 84
national_raw_news.content: A fresh flood threat is emerging in northern Odisha as the Subarnarekha continues to rise in Balasore amid persistent rain. The rainfall is being fuelled by a low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining West Bengal-north Odisha coasts, which IMD says is likely to become more marked and move west-northwestwards. IMD has warned of extremely heavy rainfall in Odisha today and tomorrow, with very heavy rain likely on Tuesday. Akashvani correspondent reports that a fresh flood threat is emerging in Balasore district as the Subarnarekha river continues to rise amid incessant rain. The river was at 8.84 metres at Rajghat, against its danger level of 10.36 metres, as last reports came in. Six gates of the Galudih Barrage in Jharkhand have been opened, raising concerns of a further rise in the river. Low-lying areas of Jaleswar, Bhograi and Baliapal could face fresh inundation. The rainfall is linked to a low-pressure area over the northwest Bay of Bengal and adjoining the West Bengal-north Odisha coasts. IMD says the system is likely to become more marked and move west-northwestwards during the next 48 hours. Extremely heavy rain is forecast in Odisha today and tomorrow, followed by very heavy rain on September first.
